![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14193775/assets/72befb19f4f9f7834c673794cece69d7d3c70da2d2b83feb4a2961c7ef1b12d3.png)

The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${q}^{′}(-1)$ where $q(x)=f(x)-g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
The addition and constant multiple rules for derivatives give

$$
{q}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)-{g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{q}^{′}(-1)={f}^{′}(-1)-{g}^{′}(-1).
$$

Also, notice that $x=-1$ corresponds to 

- the interval $x\in (-2,0)$ for the function $f,$ and

- the interval $x\in (-2,0)$ for the function $g,$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14193775/assets/244c8f29305d462ad11eabd50b9e55ae6b1de5d168d64768ed522a915aa1f283.png)

- The slope of $y=f(x)$ is constant on $x\in (-2,0)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{3-1}{0-(-2)}=1.
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(-1)=1.$

- The slope of $y=g(x)$ is constant on $x\in (-2,0)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δg}{Δx}=\frac{(-3)-1}{0-(-2)}=-2.
$$

Therefore, ${g}^{′}(-1)=-2.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}^{′}(-1) & ={f}^{′}(-1)-{g}^{′}(-1) \\  & =1-(-2) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
